candidate.answerReason: Exactly one of Carlos's three equally likely seats is opposite Angie.

methods.label: Consider Carlos's possible seats
methods.explanation:
Only Carlos's position relative to Angie matters. Wherever Angie sits, Carlos is equally likely to occupy any of the three remaining seats. These are the seat to her left, the seat to her right, and the seat opposite her. Exactly one of them is opposite her, so the probability is
\[
\frac{1}{3}.
\]
The answer is choice B.
methods.levelReason: Uses three equally likely possibilities and the elementary favorable-over-total probability rule.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is probability in an equally likely setting. Fraction meaning supports interpreting one favorable seat out of three; permutation formulas and symmetry-equivalence counting are unnecessary.
